title: Fallback comparator bug demoted Dedicated tenants to low-cost model variants
creator: Maya Patel
description: Production customer escalations: several Dedicated tenants observed an increase in latency and inference errors after being routed to lower-cost hosted model variants in different regions. The smart routing fallback comparator introduced in runtime-1.22 changed ordering semantics and allowed cross-deployment/region tie-breaks to override configured tier priority, causing misroutes for capacity-constrained Dedicated pools. This ticket tracks the triage, hotfix, verification, and postmortem actions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a request with tenant=acme-corp, preferred_region=us-west-2, tier=dedicated, model_family=redwood-ggml
2) Simulate capacity pressure: mark Dedicated pool for us-west-2 as saturated in the simulator (or reduce available slots)
3) Send 500 concurrent requests with realistic seq_len distribution (avg 256)
4) Observe routed targets in routing logs: some requests are routed to hosted eu-west-1 cheap-quantized variants instead of queued or failing over to dedicated fallback variants in the same region
5) Check comparator output: priorities serialized and compared lexicographically causing 'eu-west-1' string to win tie-breaks over numeric tier priority
root_cause: A refactor to the fallback policy comparator (commit 9f3a2d) replaced a numeric priority comparator with a generic tuple comparison that performs lexicographic string comparison on the serialized key parts. When availability score and cost_score tie, the comparator falls back to the region string which lexicographically favored non-local regions. The comparator also did not treat 'deployment_type' (hosted/dedicated/private) as a higher-order key, allowing hosted variants to win ties against Dedicated variants.
mitigation_and_fix: Hotfix deployed (runtime patch) to restore numeric priority ordering and to add explicit deployment_type precedence. Patch landed in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 and was rolled out to Hosted and Dedicated control planes.
Temporary policy override applied: forced-route rule for affected tenants to pin to dedicated pools until full verification (console rule id: FR-21567-1).
Customer communication: PM notified impacted customers and provided timeline and temporary workarounds (see support thread).
rollout_and_verification: Canary deployment to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 (03/08) — monitor routing mismatch rate and error budget impact
Full rollout across regions completed 03/10 with no regression in latency or cost metrics for affected tenants
Post-deploy verification: ran synthetic tenant workload (100k requests) and validated 0 cross-deployment misroutes and expected fallback counts
Dashboards: routing.misroute_rate dropped from 2.8% to 0.04% for affected customers within 30 minutes of fix
postmortem_actions: 1) Add unit + integration tests that exercise comparator ordering across (availability_score, cost_score, deployment_type, numeric_tier, region) — ENG-21567-tests
2) Add a chaos test in CI that injects Dedicated pool saturation and verifies no cross-deployment fallback when explicit tenant isolation is configured
3) Improve observability: add per-tenant fallback_reason tag and a high-cardinality metric for cross_deployment_routing_count
4) Update runbook: include runbook step to add forced-route and how to verify (Confluence page INC-21567 runbook), and an on-call checklist
5) Schedule design review for policy comparator API to make ordering explicit and documented (owner: Diego Ramirez, due 2026-03-25)
